answer: A mapping service stores an atlas of trellis farms. Before a public randomness beacon fires, each storage agent commits to a replica encoded for its own key. Timed audits request unpredictable blocks, with payouts proportional to verified byte-hours and no per-account bonus. Encoding must prevent one stored copy from serving many keys. A Sybil farmer must supply more disk space and bandwidth to earn more; extra names alone do nothing. This relies on sound replication proofs and audit deadlines.
